taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 0 state changes, each allowed by a review (0 reviews in all)
1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
The current HTTP Semantics specification is RFC 9110, which I read at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html. Of these twelve codes, seven are heuristically cacheable (203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414, 501) and five are not (303, 307, 413, 421, 422).

**How cacheability was decided:** Section 15.1 of the spec lists the heuristically cacheable codes: "Responses with status codes that are defined as heuristically cacheable (e.g., 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501 in this specification)". It then says that "all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable." Each code marked true below also says so in its own section. For example, §15.3.4 says "A 203 response is heuristically cacheable". The sections for 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422 have no such statement.

**One wording difference:** for 206, the spec says "unless otherwise indicated by explicit cache controls". It leaves out "the method definition", which appears in the wording for the other cacheable codes.

| Code | Reason phrase | Section | Heuristically cacheable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 203 | Non-Authoritative Information | 15.3.4 | yes |
| 206 | Partial Content | 15.3.7 | yes |
| 303 | See Other | 15.4.4 | no |
| 307 | Temporary Redirect | 15.4.8 | no |
| 308 | Permanent Redirect | 15.4.9 | yes |
| 405 | Method Not Allowed | 15.5.6 | yes |
| 410 | Gone | 15.5.11 | yes |
| 413 | Content Too Large | 15.5.14 | no |
| 414 | URI Too Long | 15.5.15 | yes |
| 421 | Misdirected Request | 15.5.20 | no |
| 422 | Unprocessable Content | 15.5.21 | no |
| 501 | Not Implemented | 15.6.2 | yes |

All quotes come from each code's own numbered section on that page. On the page the text wraps across several lines; in the quotes below I joined it with single spaces.

{"code":"203","reason":"Non-Authoritative Information","section":"15.3.4","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"This status code allows the proxy to notify recipients when a transformation has been applied, since that knowledge might impact later decisions regarding the content.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"206","reason":"Partial Content","section":"15.3.7","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"The 206 (Partial Content) status code indicates that the server is successfully fulfilling a range request for the target resource by transferring one or more parts of the selected representation.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"303","reason":"See Other","section":"15.4.4","heuristicallyCacheable":false,"quote":"This status code is applicable to any HTTP method.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"307","reason":"Temporary Redirect","section":"15.4.8","heuristicallyCacheable":false,"quote":"Since the redirection can change over time, the client ought to continue using the original target URI for future requests.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"308","reason":"Permanent Redirect","section":"15.4.9","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"The 308 (Permanent Redirect) status code indicates that the target resource has been assigned a new permanent URI and any future references to this resource ought to use one of the enclosed URIs.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"405","reason":"Method Not Allowed","section":"15.5.6","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"The origin server MUST generate an Allow header field in a 405 response containing a list of the target resource's currently supported methods.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"410","reason":"Gone","section":"15.5.11","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"The 410 (Gone) status code indicates that access to the target resource is no longer available at the origin server and that this condition is likely to be permanent.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"413","reason":"Content Too Large","section":"15.5.14","heuristicallyCacheable":false,"quote":"The 413 (Content Too Large) status code indicates that the server is refusing to process a request because the request content is larger than the server is willing or able to process.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"414","reason":"URI Too Long","section":"15.5.15","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"The 414 (URI Too Long) status code indicates that the server is refusing to service the request because the target URI is longer than the server is willing to interpret.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"421","reason":"Misdirected Request","section":"15.5.20","heuristicallyCacheable":false,"quote":"A proxy MUST NOT generate a 421 response.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"422","reason":"Unprocessable Content","section":"15.5.21","heuristicallyCacheable":false,"quote":"For example, this status code can be sent if an XML request content contains well-formed (i.e., syntactically correct), but semantically erroneous XML instructions.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"},
{"code":"501","reason":"Not Implemented","section":"15.6.2","heuristicallyCacheable":true,"quote":"This is the appropriate response when the server does not recognize the request method and is not capable of supporting it for any resource.","url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html"}
]}
